Maturity pathway

Three-year transformation roadmap

2027 FOUNDATION  →  2028 INTEGRATION  →  2029 AGENTIC

Review the move from governed standard automation, through integrated operations and AI assistance, to bounded autonomous agents. Select a card for its specific dependencies and economics.

Delivery sequencing: Maturity levels and target years are proposals, not deployment commitments. A 2029 autonomous use case still needs 2027–28 data, policy, audit, access, and rollback prerequisites.

Analyst evidence library

17 traceable references

TSIA, Omdia, ISG, IDC and McKinsey are considered alongside DORA and AWS. The model deliberately does not claim case-specific industry benchmarks where no comparable peer observation was verified.

How to read evidence strength

ObservedMeasured in a named population, methodology or selected case; applicability varies.
DirectionalMarket trends, survey results, vendor aspiration or adjacent-task comparison.
AssumedCurrent FTE, handling time, adoption and costs in this model: synthetic, unvalidated.
Evidence principle: Analyst findings are contextual comparators, not the origin of numeric current-state or target values. Verify public claims against the linked materials and commission proprietary peer benchmarks where justified.
Design safeguards & realisation

Architecture and value governance

A multi-tenant AI Ops and orchestration plane needs clean customer identity, policy isolation, evidence-backed reasoning and measurable post-execution outcomes.

Illustrative cross-domain component model

EXPERIENCECustomer / MSP service layer

Intent, request, service catalogue, SLA, value-stream outcome

INTELLIGENCEALT AI platform + model router

Customer-scoped virtual agent instance, reasoning, retrieval

CONTROLPolicy, identity & agent audit

Per-customer boundaries, HITL gates, approved tool scope

EXECUTIONReusable automation layer

IaC, API/MCP, validation, rollback, workflow evidence

DATA & VALUEOperational context / value graph

CMDB, events, telemetry, tickets, KPIs and benefit ledger

Evidence-to-value operating cycle

01 · BASELINE

Establish activity denominators

12 months of ticket, change, incident, patch and audit records by service tower and customer cohort, with sampled human touch time.

02 · ASSIGN

Make benefit pools unique

One activity belongs to one primary value pool; allocate shared investment once, and calculate only incremental benefits as new phases go live.

03 · GOVERN

Policy-gate agent permissions

Explicit execution classes, approval thresholds, tenant isolation, permitted tools, observability, evidence capture, manual fallback and rollback.

04 · PRICE

Translate effort into financials

Finance validates loaded rates, incremental platform costs, realisable savings, contract margin and any customer pricing or new service revenue.

05 · DEMONSTRATE

Prove customer outcomes

Map technical metrics to service availability, risk and request-to-fulfilment experience. Quantify customer outcomes independently of MSP time savings.

06 · OBSERVE

Close the value loop

Run monthly value scorecards. Record observed baselines and realised KPIs; revise assumptions and change, risk or adoption controls as evidence arrives.

Source architecture assumptions

Foundation: Existing Advania ALT, ServiceNow, Kaseya, CMDB, Ansible/Terraform and telemetry tools wherever identified in the use-case source.
Agent operating pattern: Shared platform management with a governed, virtualised tenant context for each customer; boundaries enforced by identity, data and tool scope.
Vendor posture: Platform-neutral first. Cisco technology and partner opportunities are assessed by capability fit and customer value, not presumed as prerequisites.

Outstanding programme validations

Technical-dependency (TD) and programme-prerequisite (PPG) IDs were preserved as identifiers. Their descriptions, critical paths and acceptance criteria must be validated with Advania architecture owners.

Human approval modes, regulatory restrictions and operational eligibility must be confirmed before moving a process from advisory to autonomous execution.
